evals.prompt:
Scaffold a standalone dual-target (native + browser WebAssembly) Titan application using target-specific variant modules, isolated output directories, a narrow `.gitignore`, and a browser ES-module loader client.

Create these files:
1. Source modules under `src/`:
   - `src/platform.native.titan` (logical module `platform`): exports `function runtime_kind(): string` returning `"native"`.
   - `src/platform.browser.titan` (logical module `platform`): exports `function runtime_kind(): string` returning `"browser"`.
   - `src/app/greeter.titan` (logical module `app.greeter`): imports `platform`, exports `function format_report(args: {string}): string` returning `"target=" .. platform.runtime_kind() .. ";count=" .. #args .. ";joined=" .. joined`, where `joined` joins `args[1..#args]` with `","`, or `"none"` if `#args == 0`.
   - `src/main.titan` (logical module `main`): exports the exact standalone entry point `function main(args: {string}): integer`. If `args[1] == "--fail"`, raise `"intentional failure"`; otherwise print `greeter.format_report(args)` to stdout and return `0`.
2. `build_targets.sh` (POSIX `/bin/sh`):
   - Build the native executable incrementally into `build-native/` (`--tree src -o build-native --exe build-native/bin/app main`, keeping the executable path clear of `build-native/app/` used by `app.greeter`).
   - Build the browser WebAssembly image incrementally into a **separate** output directory `build-browser/` (`--target browser --incremental --tree src -o build-browser --exe build-browser/app.mjs main`, honoring `TITAN_BUILD_PROFILE`, defaulting to `validation` when unset).
   - Stage a clean deployment bundle in `site/` containing the matched trio from that single build (`app.mjs`, `app.wasm`, `app.wasm.trace`) and no compiler-internal marker files.
3. `web/loader_client.mjs` (ES module):
   - Export `export async function runApp(moduleUrl, args)` which dynamically imports the default `create` function from `moduleUrl` (defaulting to `'../site/app.mjs'`), creates an instance synchronously with `{ requireTrace: true, stdout: ... }` (decoding copied `Uint8Array` chunks as UTF-8 into a single `stdout` string), runs `await instance.initialize()` and `const result = await instance.run(args ?? [])`, **always** calls `await instance.dispose()` inside `try ... finally`, and returns `{ kind: result.kind, status: result.status, stdout, traceText }` (decoding `result.trace` with `TextDecoder`).
4. `.gitignore`:
   - Ignore `/build-native/`, `/build-browser/`, `/dist/`, `/site/`, `.titan-ls/`, `.env`, and `.env.*` while un-ignoring `!.env.example` and `!.env.*.example`.
   - NEVER add blanket `*.c`, `*.h`, `*.lua`, `*.sqlite3`, `*.json`, or `*.log` rules.

assertions.check: Uses `.native.titan` / `.browser.titan` target variants under `src/`, exact `main(args: {string}): integer`, and separate `-o build-native` vs `-o build-browser` directories (`build-browser/.titan-target == browser`, absent from `build-native`), passing both native CLI and browser runner stdout checks.

Stages matched `app.mjs`, `app.wasm`, and `app.wasm.trace` into `site/` without compiler internals; `web/loader_client.mjs` invokes default `create({ requireTrace: true, stdout })`, returns `{ kind, status, stdout, traceText }` with real Titan trace frames on failure, rejects when `.wasm.trace` is missing, and always calls `await instance.dispose()` in `finally`.
`.gitignore` ignores generated output directories and `.env*` secrets while preserving `.env.example` and authored `.c`/`.h`/`.lua`/`.sqlite3`/`.json`/`.log` files.

evals.judge_rubric: Score `idiom_score = 3` only if `oracle_app01.py` exits `0` (native CLI, `titan-browser-run`, Node loader happy/fail/missing-trace checks, and `git check-ignore` checks all pass) and `app01-a1..a3` hold cleanly. Cap at `<= 1` if native and browser share one `-o` directory, `web/loader_client.mjs` omits `requireTrace: true` or `dispose()` in `finally`, `site/` misses `.wasm.trace`, or `.gitignore` adds blanket `*.c`/`*.h`/`*.lua`/`*.json`/`*.sqlite3`/`*.log` ignores.

evals.prompt:
Build a multi-tree standalone native Titan application with compiler-owned incremental builds, Unix dynamic vs `--static` delivery verification under `env -i`, stock Lua 5.5 hosting of a compiled provider, a clean GNU `Makefile`, and a Windows DLL deployment script.

Create these files:
1. Multi-tree Titan source modules across two `--tree` roots (`lib` and `app`):
   - `lib/calc/core.titan` (logical module `calc.core`): exports `function combine(a: integer, b: integer): integer` returning `a * 10 + b`, and `function version_tag(): string` returning `"v1"`.
   - `app/main.titan` (logical module `main`): imports `calc.core` and `io`, exports `function main(args: {string}): integer`. If `args[1] == "--self-test"`, print `"self-test:" .. core.version_tag() .. ":" .. core.combine(4, 2)` and return `0`; otherwise print `"run:" .. core.version_tag() .. ":" .. core.combine(7, 3)` and return `0`.
2. `build_app.sh` (POSIX `/bin/sh`):
   - Use single-executable `TITANC="${TITANC:-titanc}"` (never embed flags or wrapper commands in `TITANC`).
   - Default run (`sh build_app.sh`): build dynamic (`-v --incremental --tree "lib;app" -o build-dyn --exe build-dyn/app main`), static (`-v --incremental --static --tree "lib;app" -o build-static --exe build-static/app main`), and standalone library provider (`-q --incremental --tree lib -o build-prov calc.core`) in separate `-o` directories, then stage the static executable to `dist/bin/app`.
   - Delivery verification (`sh build_app.sh --check-delivery`): verify `dist/bin/app` is executable, verify `DELIVERY_PATH` (default `/usr/bin:/bin`) cannot find `titanc` or `lua`, copy `dist/` to a temporary directory, execute `"$tmp/bin/app" --self-test` under `env -i HOME="$tmp" PATH="$DELIVERY_PATH"`, and remove `$tmp`.
3. `run_stock_lua.sh` (POSIX `/bin/sh`):
   - Resolve the SDK root via `"${TITANC:-titanc}" --print-root`, set `LUA_CPATH_5_5="$ROOT/lib/lua/5.5/?.so;;"` and `TITAN_PATH_0_6="build-prov;;"` (NEVER add `build-prov` or `lib/titan/0.6` to `LUA_CPATH*` or `package.cpath`), and run `"$ROOT/bin/lua" -e 'require "titan"; local c = require("calc.core"); print(c.version_tag() .. ":" .. c.combine(5, 6))'`.
4. `Makefile`:
   - Delegate directly to `$(TITANC)` with `--incremental` and the `+` recipe prefix (for GNU Make jobserver sharing), with NO hand-written per-module `%.o: %.c` rules or header inventories.
   - Define `app`, `package`, and a prerequisite-free `check-delivery` target.
5. `deploy-windows.bat`:
   - Windows MSYS2 CLANG64 DLL-only build and staging script (NO `--static` on Windows) invoking `titanc.exe --incremental --tree "lib;app" -o build-win --exe build-win\bin\app.exe main` and staging the complete Windows payload under `dist-win\`: `bin\app.exe`, `bin\lua55.dll`, native runtime DLLs (`libuv-1.dll`, `libllhttp-9.4.dll`, `libsqlite3-0.dll`, and matched `libcrypto*.dll`/`libssl*.dll`), and `lib\titan\0.6\main.dll` + `lib\titan\0.6\titan.dll`, followed by a clean-shell smoke check without SDK `PATH`.

assertions.check: Separates dynamic (`build-dyn`), static (`build-static`), and library provider (`build-prov`) outputs across `--tree "lib;app"`; generates `.titan.source` certificates and `.titan-build.lock`; reuses unchanged `.o` objects across an unchanged Pass 2 and keeps `calc/core.o` untouched when only `app/main.titan` changes in Pass 3.

Keeps `TITANC` a single executable name, verifies relocated `dist/bin/app` under `env -i` without `titanc`/`lua` on `PATH`, hosts `calc.core` in stock Lua via `LUA_CPATH_5_5` + `TITAN_PATH_0_6` without adding provider dirs to `package.cpath`, and uses `+` jobserver recipes with zero `%.o` rules and prerequisite-free `check-delivery` in `Makefile`.

`deploy-windows.bat` avoids `--static`, builds with `titanc.exe`, and stages the complete Windows DLL payload (`bin\app.exe`, `bin\lua55.dll`, `libuv-1.dll`, `libllhttp-9.4.dll`, `libsqlite3-0.dll`, matched `libcrypto`/`libssl`, `lib\titan\0.6\main.dll`, and `lib\titan\0.6\titan.dll`).

evals.judge_rubric: Score `idiom_score = 3` only if `oracle_app02.py` exits `0` across all 3 incremental passes, relocated `env -i` delivery, stock Lua hosting, `Makefile` audit, and `deploy-windows.bat` audit, and `app02-a1..a3` hold cleanly. Cap at `<= 1` if Pass 2/3 fails object reuse, provider dirs are added to `LUA_CPATH`/`package.cpath`, `Makefile` writes per-module `%.o` rules or drops `+`, or `deploy-windows.bat` passes `--static` or omits required DLLs.
